items.calibration: using GdSi as standards and also removing of the oxide layer on the sample surface by ion sputtering
items.quote: The quantitative analysis of individual phases was done by energy-dispersive spectroscopy (EDS) on a JEOL 7830F Auger Microprobe. An uncertainty less than ±1% was obtained by using GdSi as standards and also removing of the oxide layer on the sample surface by ion sputtering.

items.calibration: calibrated against the melting points of pure In and Al
items.crucible: wrapped with tantalum foils then crimped in a copper pan
items.quote: Due to the weak signal of the polymorphic transition in the silicides, some of the alloys were analyzed in a differential scanning calorimeter (DSC). The thermocouples used in the DSC were calibrated against the melting points of pure In and Al and the accuracy of the temperature was estimated to be within ±2 ◦ C. DSC measurements were carried out on samples wrapped with tantalum foils then crimped in a copper pan. The measurements were conducted between room temperature and 700 ◦ C.

items.method: optical microscopy or scanning electron microscopy (SEM)
items.quote: The microstructure of the annealed samples was investigated by optical microscopy or scanning electron microscopy (SEM).

items.atmosphere: Ar atmosphere gettered by Zr at 600 ◦ C with a flow rate of 50 cm3 /min
items.calibration: calibrated to the transition temperature of high purity K2 SO4 and the melting point of Au
items.quote: The differential thermal analysis investigations were carried out in a Perkin Elmer DTA 7 which can reach a maximum temperature of 1500 ◦ C. The thermocouples were calibrated to the transition temperature of high purity K2 SO4 and the melting point of Au and the temperature measured were accurate to within ±5 ◦ C. For the measurements, samples weighing 20-60 mg were cycled at heating and cooling rates of 10 ◦ C/min in tantalum crucibles under an Ar atmosphere gettered by Zr at 600 ◦ C with a flow rate of 50 cm3 /min.

X-ray diffraction studies were conducted in a Philips X'Pert PRO diffractometer with Cu K␣ radiation at 45 kV and 40 mA. Scans were typically taken over a 2θ range of 20-90◦ using a scan step of 0.02◦ .

items.applies_to: alloys with a composition range from 30 to 65 at.% Si
items.calibration: calibrated to the melting point of platinum
items.crucible: tantalum crucibles with an embedded thermocouple well
items.quote: In order to investigate the liquidus and melting ranges of alloys with a composition range from 30 to 65 at.% Si, additional thermal analysis was conducted. Alloys were arc-melted, homogenized and sealed in tantalum crucibles with an embedded thermocouple well. Tungsten-Rhenium Type C thermocouples calibrated to the melting point of platinum were used for temperature measurement. Niobium held in a second crucible was used as a reference. The voltages from the two thermocouples were recorded at the same time during heating and cooling. The liquidus temperature was obtained when the difference in voltages is a maximum from the two thermocouples.

items.label: Alloys
items.quote: Alloys were prepared from high purity elemental Gd and Si. The Gd was supplied by the Materials Preparation Center [25] at the Ames Laboratory and it was (99.995 wt.%) pure. The major impurities in ppm by weight were as follows: O, 155; C, 49; Si, 36; Cl, 36; S, 34; and single crystal Si with a purity of 99.9999 at.%. All alloys were formed by arc melting appropriate amounts of the constituent elements.
